validated_results.title: Associations of intakes of total protein, protein from dairy sources, and dietary calcium with risks of colorectal, breast, and prostate cancer: a prospective analysis in UK Biobank.
validated_results.reason: Prospective UK Biobank cohort reporting a positive association between dietary calcium intake and incident prostate cancer with a quantitative hazard ratio.

extraction.comparison_type: Quartile 4 vs Quartile 1 of dietary calcium intake
extraction.population: UK Biobank participants who completed at least two 24-h dietary assessments

sample_size.excerpt: Using a subsample of UK Biobank participants who completed ≥2 (maximum of 5) 24-h dietary assessments, we estimated intakes of total protein, protein from total dairy products, milk, and cheese, and dietary calcium in 114,217 participants.

cases.excerpt: After a median of 9.4 years of follow-up, 1193 colorectal, 2024 female breast, and 2422 prostate cancer cases were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: We also observed positive associations of milk protein and dietary calcium with prostate cancer risk (HR<sub>Q4 vs Q1</sub>:1.12, 1.00-1.26 and 1.16, 1.01-1.33, respectively).

confidence_interval.excerpt: There were inverse associations of total dairy protein, protein from milk, and dietary calcium intakes with colorectal cancer incidence (HR<sub>Q4 vs Q1</sub>:0.80, 95% CI: 0.67-0.94; 0.79, 0.67-0.94; 0.71, 0.58-0.86, respectively). We also observed positive associations of milk protein and dietary calcium with prostate cancer risk (HR<sub>Q4 vs Q1</sub>:1.12, 1.00-1.26 and 1.16, 1.01-1.33, respectively).

design.excerpt: a prospective analysis in UK Biobank

timing.excerpt: After a median of 9.4 years of follow-up

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
